concerns.text: T005's verification is `grep -q "full family" specs/001-quantifying-disorder-effect/plan.md`, but the plan.md under review still reads "Bonferroni correction for pairwise comparisons only" (Summary) and "Applied to pairwise width comparisons" (coverage matrix). The task asserts "plan.md was updated accordingly and committed" — a completed-work claim with no evidence, and the verification command cannot pass against the current plan text. Either the plan edit must actually land or the verification must not depend on prose in another document.

T004 bundles at least four separable deliverables into one task: the full W×L×realizations sweep, the PR(L) saturation fitting per W, the W=0 edge-case handling, and the merge into scaling_fits.json with failure logging. Each has distinct verification. Too coarse — split so each deliverable is independently verifiable (the atomizer will otherwise have to guess the boundaries).

T002 spans Hamiltonian generation, PR analysis, sparse-solver fallback, HDF5 storage with checksums/provenance, and a JSON-lines numerical logger — five modules with one verification clause. Too coarse for deterministic execution; split by module (e.g., generation+storage vs. PR analysis vs. logger).

T008 combines plotting, localization-center identification, log-linear fitting, quantitative summaries in four named doc sections, and a plain-prose narrative. Too coarse; the doc-writing and the fitting/plotting deliverables have different verifications and should be separate tasks.
T009 merges edge-case unit tests, a performance benchmark with resource caps, and an end-to-end validation report into one task. Too coarse; each is independently verifiable and should be split.

T006's convergence criterion is cited as "FR:" with no FR number — the implementer cannot trace which requirement governs the ≤5% relative-change threshold. Name the FR/SC id (it appears to derive from US-2 scenario 2).
